method: Create one user-authorized temporary Codex task using the configured default model.
The real agent posts through the CLI fallback into an isolated database using its actual task ID.
Observe the first turn complete and task status become idle; no operator_wait lease is used.
Discover the existing desktop conversation owner without sending a follow-up.
Programmatically activate the production QML Approve button in the existing shell. The test hides the popup window.
The unchanged watcher dispatcher delivers the saved approval through local Codex desktop IPC.
Observe a second real agent turn, its CLI response read and exact-ID acknowledgement, and a completed verification receipt.
Compare task ID, request ID, response ID and per-test nonce with the original request and native panel state.
Remove the isolated native test plugin and archive the temporary Codex task.
limits: One local task with a discoverable owner on the recorded Codex desktop build.
The desktop IPC interface is internal and version-sensitive.
UI activation was automated; the popup was hidden to avoid interfering with current desktop work.
The request and acknowledgement used CLI fallback with isolated data; registered MCP tools were tested separately.
This test does not verify Claude/Hermes desktop modes or other Codex conversation states.
